record_reviews.summary: Darwin declines an invitation to dine at Downing College because influenza and a bad cough make him too unwell.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: An invitation is the antecedent, but no incoming letter or named correspondent is preserved.

evidence.quote: I was so unwell all yesterday with a bad cough

record_reviews.summary: Darwin’s Geological Society report recommends shortening and publishing David Williams’s raised-beach paper after Sedgwick and Murchison because it supports their conclusions and adds evidence from barnacles, a subsided forest and changed gravel beds.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Secure single day, 27 March 1837.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin is the report writer/signatory; Williams, Sedgwick and Murchison’s arguments are summarized as the subject of the official report.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: This is an official referee recommendation about a paper, not a response to a surviving incoming letter.

evidence.quote: The chief point of additional evidence is the discovery of numerous barnacles

record_reviews.summary: Darwin recommends Forchhammer’s communication on Danish changes of level for the Transactions, citing its evidence about beaches, shells, deposits and submarine forests and suggesting an accompanying diagram.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Secure single day, 20 October 1837; the footnote records the communication was read 31 May 1837, which is not the report’s composition date.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The report evaluates an external Geological Society communication; no surviving incoming prompt exists.

evidence.quote: appears to me worthy of place in the Transactions

record_reviews.summary: The surviving catalogue text says Darwin asks whether the recipient prefers the President’s signature alone or signatures of other scientific men; the original body is not supplied.

evidence.quote: Asks correspondent if he would prefer the President’s signature alone or with those of other scientific men

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks an unidentified correspondent to obtain permission for another visit to Addiscombe to inspect the St Helena model before his geology goes to press, so he can correct section proportions.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Single editorially supplied day, 12 September [1838].
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes the body; the recipient remains unidentified despite the referenced Clark and Addiscombe authorities.

record_reviews.summary: A surviving final-page fragment says the recipient’s lectures are going well and thanks them; the beginning and recipient are missing.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin supplies a detailed character reference for Syms Covington, describing his Beagle service, clerical work, handwriting, prudence, economy and sobriety.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Secure single day, 29 May 1839.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes/signs the recommendation; Covington’s employment history is reported by Darwin.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The application or request for this reference is not preserved, and no recipient is identified as a packet correspondent.

evidence.quote: I have known Syms Covington for more than eight years

record_reviews.summary: Darwin’s Geological Society recommendation says Clarke’s report of volcanic ash falling aboard the Roxburgh is fully represented in the Proceedings and need not be printed in the Transactions.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin resigns as a Geological Society secretary because of ill health, explaining that regret delayed the step and offering to continue attending if replacement is delayed.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Secure single day, 24 March 1840; the editorial footnote says the letter was read by Council on 25 March.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes/signs the individual resignation to the President and Council; the Council and its office are institutional recipients.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The Council’s subsequent request and response are outside this packet; 562 is a later response to that missing communication, not a prompt that can be attributed to 561 alone.

evidence.quote: I feel myself compelled, from the state of my health to resign the office of one of your secretaries

record_reviews.summary: Darwin agrees reluctantly to remain Geological Society secretary until the next anniversary after Council’s request, while recording his continuing wish to resign because illness prevents attendance.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Secure single day, 28 March [1840]; the footnote records Council read it on 8 April, a later institutional event.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes/signs the individual response; “the Council” and its prior communication are institutional, missing voices.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: 561 is Darwin’s earlier resignation, but 562 answers a subsequent Council communication not preserved here; the two outgoing letters are not treated as a direct pair.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The Council letter requesting continuation is absent, so 562’s institutional prompt cannot be reconstructed from 561.

evidence.quote: I feel that I have no choice in complying with the request of the Council
I cannot hold the office, which although so honourable to me, I have found very irksome, beyond the next anniversary

record_reviews.summary: A two-paragraph autograph-album scrap says Darwin cannot advise on separation of the sexes in guanaco and signs off; the address and recipient are incomplete.

record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes/signs the surviving scrap; addressee is unresolved and no other voice is present.

issues: All 21 packet records were read in full, including every retained body paragraph, header, metadata date audit/constraints, editorial summary and editorial footnotes. Preserved HTML text was read directly; metadata has_transcription_in_preserved_xml:false was not treated as absence of an HTML body.

No direct reply links are proposed. Geological Society items are official reports/recommendations or institutional letters; unidentified items lack recipients or antecedent texts. Embedded papers, memoirs, invitations and catalogue extracts are not substituted for missing incoming letters.

DCP-LETT-612 is joint committee writing signed by four people; Darwin’s signature does not establish sole authorship. DCP-LETT-13864 and DCP-LETT-13865 are bracketed/catalogue extracts and are explicitly limited as non-full originals, while 13925F and 570F are surviving fragments.
DCP-LETT-561 and 562 are separate Darwin outgoing institutional letters. 562 responds to an unpreserved Council request after 561; it is not treated as a 561 prompt or direct pair.

No cross-correspondent source/witness record in all_letters.jsonl supplied a unique prompt or knowledge link for these records; official paper subjects and unidentified recipients remain external or unresolved. Additional Council communications, original manuscripts/extracts, invitations, and administrative replies would be needed for stronger links.
